scenes.title: The Valve With Old Initials
scenes.storyBeat: An old quick patch worsens the candy pressure loop.
storyboardPanels: A brass pressure valve puffs sugar steam.
Zuzu spots Z.Z. scratched into the metal.

preChoiceDialogue.text: Terrible, but interesting. Parade-strength frosting in a sewer-rated pipe.
Emergency handwriting. Limited supervision. Excellent confidence.

choices.label: Tighten the Sprinkle Valve
choices.playerLine: Stop the part currently screaming. Pretend the initials are historical graffiti.
choices.narration: Zuzu clamps the valve and drops the sticky pressure.

choices.label: Log the Pressure Fault
choices.playerLine: If my patch caused this, the repair says so in ink big enough for future goblins to resent.

npcResponse.text: Previous note found: temporary sugar-flow shortcut. Expired three festivals ago.

choices.narration: Zuzu reads the note instead of hiding it. The valve obeyed a shortcut for far too long.
choices.gameplayResult: Sticky warnings become easier to read.

choices.label: Overclock the Candy Pump
choices.playerLine: Route the excess through a controlled sparkle burst and harvest candy kinetic optimism.
choices.narration: A ribbon of sprinkle light clears sticky patches before the tunnel hiccups out fresh frosting.

postChoiceBarks.text: Sprinkle flow now within legal joy limits. Probably.

victoryCallback.text: Sewer stable. Initials unexploded. Graph trending.

bossCallback.text: The slimes followed pressure, not orders. Beautiful chain. Slightly embarrassing chain.

scenes.title: The Override Still Running
scenes.storyBeat: Prototype No. 7 exposes a hidden override Zuzu avoided documenting.
storyboardPanels: Zuzu's old intern bench still smokes.
A receipt prints OVERRIDE STILL ACTIVE.
Junk blocks line up in the warning tray.

preChoiceDialogue.text: My beloved terrible bench. Each scorch mark represents learning or insufficient ventilation.
Temporary override has operated continuously for two years.
That is a very committed temporary.

choices.label: Clamp the Rattle Belt
choices.playerLine: Contain first, confess later. The belt stops donating junk to columns.
choices.narration: Zuzu clamps the conveyor and slows the junk queue.

choices.label: Open the Intern Ledger
choices.playerLine: No heroic wrenching until I read the ledger.

npcResponse.text: Entry found: remove override before final celebration. Removal status: not removed.

choices.narration: Zuzu goes quiet for three whole seconds, which is a public ceremony in goblin engineering.

choices.label: Boot Prototype No. 7 1/2
choices.playerLine: Launch a legally distinct helper prototype. Machines respect peer review.

npcResponse.text: Machines do not respect peer review.

choices.narration: Version 7 1/2 redirects junk, then sneezes a spring into the hold queue.

postChoiceBarks.text: Prototype behavior reduced from catastrophic to educational.

victoryCallback.text: Override noted. Pride dented. Repair improved.

bossCallback.text: No more blaming the machine. I left the override in. Now we fix it.

scenes.title: The Thaw Protocol
scenes.storyBeat: The pantry needs a proper thaw protocol.
storyboardPanels: A copper coil hums inside an icebox.
The active piece freezes, then drops too fast.
A label says DO NOT HUG.

preChoiceDialogue.text: Thermal device alternating between chill and dramatic panic. Classic unhelpful helpfulness.
Do not reverse it too quickly.
Fine. Protocol instead of theatrical polarity. Growth is inconvenient.

choices.label: Rewire the Thaw Relay
choices.playerLine: Relay first. Less drama, fewer frozen eyebrows.
choices.narration: Zuzu rewires the relay and steadies the worst speed swings.

choices.label: Write the Thaw Protocol
choices.playerLine: Step one: ask pantry. Step two: label heat. Step three: no surprise soup.
choices.narration: The pantry receives instructions that future goblins can read before touching the coil.

choices.label: Reverse Snowcone Polarity
choices.playerLine: Educational reversal, tiny scale, excellent goggles.
choices.narration: The coil bursts into glittering frost and spits rare parts across the shelf.

postChoiceBarks.text: Documentation is engineering that talks after you leave.

bossCallback.text: Gelato Golem, we have a protocol. It includes fewer dramatic freezes.

scenes.title: The Quiet Warranty
scenes.storyBeat: A pillow alarm must be repaired with consent, not forced testing.
storyboardPanels: A plush alarm clicks under blankets.
Sleepy guards wear tiny consent ribbons.
Zuzu holds a very loud spring.

preChoiceDialogue.text: Alarm status: fixable. Resident status: asleep and not volunteers.
New rule. No participants by accident.

choices.label: Muffle the Gearbox
choices.playerLine: Felt pads. Soft clamps. No heroic clang.
choices.narration: Zuzu muffles the gearbox and stabilizes the sleepy room.

choices.label: Issue a Quiet Warranty
choices.playerLine: Warranty clause: no sudden bells without resident approval.

npcResponse.text: Consent clause archived. Alarm humility increased.

choices.narration: The alarm learns to ask before helping, which makes the whole castle less tense.

choices.label: Launch the Pillow Spring
choices.playerLine: One tiny launch. Educational arc. Soft landing assumed.

npcResponse.text: Pillow trajectory filed under brave upholstery.

choices.narration: The spring launches a pillow into a perfect defensive bounce and wakes one curtain.

postChoiceBarks.text: The lever is reachable. Drama reduced. Fine.

victoryCallback.text: Alarm repaired. No accidental test subjects.

bossCallback.text: Sir Snore-a-Lot, all wake-up features now require permission.

scenes.title: The Formula Behind the Lights
scenes.storyBeat: The score formula must become fair instead of mysterious.
storyboardPanels: A score cabinet hides its math behind prize curtains.
Zuzu finds a locked formula panel.

preChoiceDialogue.text: This game is obeying secret math. Secret math near prizes is suspicious math.
Mystery is not a balancing tool. It is a hiding place with fonts.

choices.label: Cap the Prize Multiplier
choices.playerLine: Multiplier cap first. Fewer jackpot tantrums.
choices.narration: Zuzu caps the cabinet's wildest score jumps.

choices.label: Share the Score Formula
choices.playerLine: Open the panel. Everyone gets to know how the points happen.

npcResponse.text: Formula visibility improved. Arcade fairness rising.

choices.narration: Players finally see why cascades score and why some lights were hogging attention.

choices.label: Run the Jackpot Spiral
choices.playerLine: One supervised spiral. Fine print glowing. Fingers away from jackpot mouth.
choices.narration: The cabinet showers tickets and immediately demands a harder combo.

postChoiceBarks.text: Fair games still explode with joy. They just warn you first.

victoryCallback.text: Score formula readable. Profit mystery sulking.

bossCallback.text: Hydra, no hidden multiplier. Everyone gets the formula.

scenes.locationName: Bloxley's Block Palace - Royal Clamp Gate
scenes.title: The Clamp Patent Problem
scenes.storyBeat: Royal clamps reveal the cost of clever design without safety notes.
storyboardPanels: Royal seals lock a gate with elegant brass clamps.
The board narrows with pattern warnings.

preChoiceDialogue.text: My palace holds because every corner obeys!
That clamp profile. That smug little pressure notch.
I made it to help stalls stand quickly. He used it to make rooms stop arguing.

choices.label: Unscrew the Royal Brackets
choices.playerLine: Remove brackets, loosen seals, stop the board becoming a filing cabinet.
choices.narration: Zuzu unscrews the brackets and downgrades several royal blocks.

choices.label: Invalidate the Clamp Patent
choices.playerLine: Any clamp that silences a room gets a release lever anyone can reach.

npcResponse.text: Public safety revision accepted. Accessibility lever required.

choices.narration: Zuzu stamps the blueprint with a red revision mark. The seals become answerable.

choices.label: Detonate Corner Theory

npcResponse.text: You would explode a royal corner?

choices.narration: The blast pops royal blocks into confetti, and the palace retaliates with stricter square rules.

postChoiceBarks.text: Corners still legal, but no longer in charge.

bossCallback.text: I built a thing that made control too easy. That part is mine. Locking people in was yours.
